title: Native input attachments can silently clip individual long JSON lines
problem: The proposed native @file route uses ReadTool, whose 2,000-character line cap can omit source values despite a small file and whole-file truncated=false. The retained d7 compact JSON packet has long lines and is unsafe to reuse unchanged as this type of attachment.
root_cause: Pinned OpenCode1.19.3 read.ts applies substring(0,2000) to an overlong line without setting its flags.more or flags.cut fields.
historical_qualification: D7 actually used bash cat for the complete packet read, not this @file input path; that retained native read was complete. This newly found attachment hazard is not relabeled as the cause of d7 timeouts.
resolution_summary: New d8 bundle inserts JSON whitespace only at punctuation outside strings; every JSON source value and all four non-JSON bodies remain complete. Before inference, the actual installed native client noReply route read the packet and all numbered lines were independently reconstructed exactly.
current_boundary: Native named-command generation remains NOT_RUN in d8. Root must still verify actual server memory, first-request token budget including wrappers/system/tool schemas, and full subsequent output/history reserve before invocation. This is not artifact-generation acceptance.
